title: Your C is not standard C
summary: This article explores the misconception that C code is truly 'standard' and portable, revealing how compilers like GCC and Clang implement the ISO C standard differently. The author demonstrates that the C standard intentionally leaves many behaviors undefined or implementation-defined, meaning most 'standard C' code is actually compiler-specific.
problem_solved: Explains why C code that follows the standard may still behave differently across compilers and platforms due to undefined and implementation-defined behaviors.
why_valuable: Helps C developers understand the practical reality of writing portable code by recognizing what the standard actually guarantees versus what compilers decide.
